integrator-customer: hey team, hitting invalid JSON from structured mode when our data contains emojis and literal \\n sequences. model: gptx-4-instruct, structured_mode=true. payload below, parser throws 'Unexpected token' on our side. any ideas?
maria: sorry you're blocked — can you paste a minimal repro and curl so we can reproduce? :hugging_face:
integrator-customer: sure -- reduced case: prompt contains a user note with a raw backslash-n plus a sombrero emoji (U+1F920). output is supposed to be JSON array of items but the model returns: 
```
{"items": ["note: line1\\nline2", "emoji: \ud83e\udd20"]}some trailing
```
we see an extra literal \"some trailing\" concatenated and our json parser fails at the tag. server returned 200 though. thread_ts=1793456789
kevin: thanks — odd that there's trailing text. does this happen only during streaming? are you using streaming=true on the client?
integrator-customer: yes streaming=true. with streaming=false it usually works but much slower and still hits rare failures. reproduces 3/10 runs for us.
maria: assigning to eng. @kevin can you look? attach the curl they used.
kevin: grabbing the curl: 
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.dev/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-4-instruct","structured_mode":true,"stream":true,"input":"Please return JSON array of notes. note: contains literal \\\\n and emoji 😜"}'
```
kevin: repro locally against canary runtime — intermittent but I hit it. stack: parser error when assembling streaming chunks: "Unexpected token <char> at pos 289". root cause looks like a split within a UTF-8 multi-byte sequence or escaped surrogate pair broken across chunks.
sylvie: that jives with previous streaming boundary bug where the assembler concatenated chunks without validating UTF-8 codepoint boundaries. if a surrogate pair (4-byte UTF-8) is split, JSON escapes can end up like "\\ud83e" + next chunk "\\udd20" becoming two separate escapes and then post-processing produced a literal "\\ud83e\\udd20" which some parsers treat differently.
kevin: logging from runtime: 
```
[2027-02-14T18:03:12Z] chunk 5: "...\\u", chunk 6: "dd20}]}}some trailing"
[2027-02-14T18:03:12Z] assembled: "...\\uddd20}]}}some trailing"  <-- malformed escape
```
maria: omg. thanks for the logs. customer impact: parsing failures and some extra trailing tokens. certainty: high.
kevin: temporary workaround for customers: disable streaming (stream=false) or post-process by extracting the first top-level JSON object/array with a tolerant parser, or ask model to emit a clear delimiter token after JSON like "<END_JSON>" then strip trailing. also escape input newlines: replace literal backslash-n with actual newline or double-escape.
integrator-customer: can you confirm a rollout plan? blocking our prod rollout.
sylvie: plan: patch assembler to buffer and validate UTF-8 boundaries before merging chunks, and normalize escapes across chunk boundary. small fix landed on branch streaming-fix-utf; PR #4321. canary rollout tonight to 3% on canary, then 25% in 2 hours if no regressions.
kevin: ETA for prod: 2027-02-15 morning (UTC). I'll attach repro test and a unit test for surrogate split.
maria: sending repro to you in DM. in the meantime we've advised customer to set stream=false or use delimiter method. :white_check_mark:
sylvie: note for runbook: add a check in the console's structured-output validator to flag malformed escapes and offer recommended mitigation automatically in the error message.
kevin: also filed a short-term SDK patch to automatically buffer 1kb before attempting to parse streaming JSON blocks (sdk-2.7.1-beta). customers using official SDKs will get this sooner.
integrator-customer: thanks all — will try stream=false and report back. appreciate the quick triage. :pray:
support-bot: Incident created: INC-20270214-78 — linked to this thread.
